title: Rates, equations, units and what data can identify
prerequisites: Stages 01, 10 and the rates primer. Review matrices and the chain rule; no prior mechanics is assumed.
data_role: Observed NIST copper measurements; manufactured cosine derivative checks. Temperature is not a time axis.
questions: Why is the first-column ordering not enough to define a time axis?
Ordering is a data operation. An axis is time only if its measurement definition establishes time; the NIST predictor is temperature in kelvin.
Derive the centered-difference leading order for a smooth function.
Subtract Taylor expansions at ±h; even powers cancel and division by 2h leaves f′+h²f‴/6+O(h⁴), with sufficient smoothness.
Which part of m and k can the unit mass-spring acceleration identify?
The equation depends on k/m. Without another measurement, scaling both by the same positive factor leaves the trajectory unchanged.
Give a zero-residual but wrong-answer example.
For u″=0, any affine function has zero interior residual. If the intended problem has u(0)=0 and u(1)=1, u=0 has zero interior residual but the wrong right boundary.
What is the NIST excerpt suitable for and unsuitable for?
Suitable: exploring static response versus temperature and held-out regression. Unsuitable: measured time integration, diffusivity identification, or replication of full-data certified statistics.
What happens if observation noise stays fixed while difference spacing shrinks?
Noise in the numerator is divided by a smaller spacing, so derivative variance can increase even as smooth truncation bias decreases.
recall: What are state, residual and identifiability?
A state contains modeled predictive information; a residual measures violation of an equation; identifiability distinguishes parameter choices from observations.
When is halving h useful?
When smooth truncation error dominates and the assumed finite-difference expansion is valid; not automatically with noisy data or roundoff.
What quantity is missing from the copper table for an ODE trajectory?
A time-resolved state and relevant forcing/initial conditions; temperature-indexed response is not such a trajectory.

title: Smooth flows, coordinate changes and invertible networks
prerequisites: Stage 13 and Stage 21; remember the difference between a function and its inverse.
data_role: Measured Iris feature pairs transformed by a chosen invertible map; the flow itself is a mathematical construction.
questions: Why is x³ not a diffeomorphism of the usual smooth real line?
The map is smooth and bijective, but its cube-root inverse is not differentiable at zero.
For x0=2, can the flow of x′=x² be evaluated at t=1 along its original solution?
No. Its maximal forward solution blows up at t=0.5; the algebraic fraction beyond that is not a continuation through the singularity.
Write the inverse affine coupling.
Keep the first coordinate x, then use (y_new-0.5 sin x)*exp(-0.2 tanh x).
Derive the log determinant of the coupling.
The Jacobian is triangular with diagonal (1,exp(s(x))); log absolute determinant is s(x).
Does a good round trip on Iris establish a biological flow?
No. It establishes an implementation property of a constructed transformation of measured features.
Does an invertible nonlinear transformation preserve a Euclidean persistence diagram exactly?
Not generally. It may alter distances and therefore the scale at which simplices enter.
recall: What extra assumption turns local flow into all-time flow?
A suitable completeness condition; smoothness alone is insufficient.
Why does normalization not have an ambient inverse?
All positive radial multiples map to the same unit vector.
What sign accompanies log determinant in the transformed density?
Subtract log abs det DF when expressing log p_Y(F(x)) from log p_X(x).

title: Mechanics, Hamiltonian networks and Lagrangian networks
prerequisites: Stages 01, 13, 21 and the neural-network paragraph in Primer 07.
data_role: Manufactured oscillator derivative data for training; observed copper data used to examine what is and is not identifiable.
questions: With m=2 and v=3, what is p?
For L=m v²/2-V(q), p=m v=6. This relation is model-specific.
Derive H for the quadratic spring Lagrangian.
Use v=p/m in pv-(m v²/2-kq²/2) to obtain p²/(2m)+kq²/2.
What condition allows the regular LNN acceleration formula?
Invertibility of the velocity Hessian; in one coordinate L_vv must be nonzero.
Which constant cannot derivative supervision identify in H?
Any additive constant; its derivative is zero.
Why can conserved learned H still describe wrong dynamics?
Many different scalar functions generate Hamiltonian dynamics. Structure alone does not identify the measured system or eliminate model error.
What is deliberately restricted in the trained LNN?
Unit kinetic term v²/2 is fixed. Only a one-coordinate potential network is learned; a general velocity-dependent L is not trained.
recall: Explain canonical momentum without saying it is always velocity.
It is partial L/partial velocity; m*v only in the stated elementary kinetic model.
What is conserved by the exact autonomous HNN flow?
The learned H, under its differentiability/canonical assumptions; not automatically measured energy or its discrete approximation.
What is the damping energy balance?
H′=-gamma*p² for the unit oscillator, so energy decreases for positive damping away from zero velocity.

title: Symplectic integration, energy, phase and long rollouts
prerequisites: Stages 14 and 23; matrix multiplication and determinant checks.
data_role: Manufactured oscillator trajectories with exact reference; a measured sunspot delay cloud used as a negative control against invented energy claims.
questions: Compute one symplectic Euler step from (1,0), h=0.2.
p_new=-0.2; q_new=0.96; energy=0.4808, different from 0.5.
What exactly does M^T J M=J establish?
Preservation of the canonical symplectic form by that linear update, not exact conservation of an arbitrary Hamiltonian.
Why is determinant one insufficient in four dimensions?
Volume preservation is weaker. diag(2,0.5,1,1) preserves total determinant but scales canonical q/p pair areas incorrectly.
Can exact energy coexist with phase error?
Yes. Implicit midpoint preserves the oscillator quadratic energy but advances by 2 atan(h/2), not the exact angle h.
Why hold the horizon fixed when testing convergence?
Otherwise changes in total simulated duration confound step-size error comparisons.
Does a sunspot delay-loop radius represent energy?
Not without a justified model, canonical state mapping and physical units; the supplied time series does not establish those.
recall: Name three independent rollout diagnostics.
Energy deviation, phase/state error and symplectic defect; also horizon, coverage and runtime.
Does symplectic mean every step size is stable?
No. Even the elementary oscillator has stability restrictions.
What is the exact continuous Hamiltonian conservation argument?
For autonomous differentiable H, grad H transposed times skew J times grad H is zero along its exact generated flow.

title: Constraints, projections, retractions and rank failure
prerequisites: Stages 13, 14, 23 and 24; review kernels, rank and tangent spaces.
data_role: Measured Iris vectors subjected to an explicitly chosen unit-sphere normalization; exact and nonlinear constraint counterexamples.
questions: For z=(2,0), calculate one unit-circle correction and the remaining residual.
A=[4,0], C=3, correction=(-0.75,0); result (1.25,0), residual 0.5625.
When is the linear correction exact?
For an affine constraint with a full-row-rank A in exact arithmetic; floating-point residual still needs checking.
Why reject the sphere origin?
The constraint Jacobian is zero and a unique radial projection direction is absent.
What is required of v in the sphere retraction?
q is a unit point and v is tangent, so q dot v=0.
Does unit norm of the normalized Iris data verify a biological law?
No. It verifies a selected preprocessing constraint, which deliberately removes radial information.
Why is a generic projection not a symplectic integrator?
It can discard dimensions or alter canonical pair relationships; it lacks the derived mechanical update and constraint-force treatment.
recall: What symbol do we use for the constraint Jacobian?
A=DC, distinct from canonical symplectic J.
Name three projection failure checks.
Constraint compatibility, Jacobian rank/conditioning, and residual/iteration convergence; also correction size.
Does feasibility imply correct motion?
No; speed, phase, energy balance, momentum, forcing and measured correspondence still need evaluation.

title: Physics-informed learning and inverse problems
prerequisites: Stages 21–25; derivatives, matrix solves, loss and training/evaluation splits.
data_role: Actual residual-trained network on a manufactured Poisson problem; separate measured NIST response-regression exercise.
questions: Verify the manufactured Poisson solution.
u=sin(pi*x) has u″=-pi² sin(pi*x), so -u″ equals the forcing and both endpoints vanish.
Which condition does x(1-x)N(x) enforce exactly?
The two homogeneous Dirichlet endpoint values, for finite N. It does not enforce the differential equation everywhere.
Why is create_graph needed for residual training through derivatives?
Training parameters must influence derivatives, so the differentiation computation itself must remain differentiable for backpropagation.
What information can a low training residual fail to provide?
Boundary correctness, off-grid error, parameter identifiability, measurement fit, and empirical generalization.
If x=L*x_hat and u=U*u_hat, how does u″ scale?
u″=(U/L²)*d²u_hat/dx_hat². Leaving out the factor changes physical units and residual weights.
Why not compare the NIST excerpt SSE with the published certified full-data SSE?
The observation count, selection and possibly model differ; the official certificate concerns the original 236-row specified benchmark.
recall: What is a collocation point?
A location at which a differential residual is evaluated, not necessarily a measured example.
What baseline should precede a neural PDE claim here?
The analytic solution and the ordinary finite-difference solve.
Does a hard boundary ansatz prove a correct PDE solution?
No. Boundary feasibility and interior solution accuracy remain distinct.

title: Conflicting gradients, interfaces, separability and PIKANs
prerequisites: Stages 21 and 26; inner products, gradients and simple linear regression.
data_role: Exact gradient examples and manufactured subdomain seams; opposing objectives derived from observed NIST regression groups.
questions: What sign of g_i dot d predicts local improvement under theta-eta*d?
Positive, with a sufficiently small step and appropriate smoothness. The actual finite-step loss still needs checking.
What is normalized in the supplied Norm-PCGrad implementation?
Each row after its sequence of projections, before summing; vanishing rows contribute zero under the declared convention.
Prove that exact opposing nonzero gradients have no strict common descent.
Their inner products with any d are negatives of each other, so they cannot both be positive.
Why inspect sequential multi-gradient outputs rather than trust a label?
Later projections can change earlier alignments and the order matters; actual dot products disclose remaining conflict.
Calculate the interface jump for the two Poisson functions.
At x=0.5 the added right term is 0.1; its derivative is -0.2, so value and slope/flux matching fail despite zero interior residuals.
Does a separable network make a dense nx-by-ny output linear in grid length?
No. Axis evaluations may be reduced, but materializing all dense entries requires quadratic storage/work in equal grid sizes.
recall: Distinguish architecture, loss and optimizer.
Architecture defines the function class; the loss encodes desired agreement; the optimizer changes parameters to reduce that objective.
Does least-squares ConFIG compatibility decide every possible common-descent question?
No. It diagnoses the specified equal-alignment system; other directional feasibility is a separate question.
Which published experiments did we reproduce?
None of the full XPINN/SPINN/PIKAN benchmark suite. We ran explicit vector, interface and factorization teaching experiments.

title: Functions to functions: DeepONet, Fourier operators and baselines
prerequisites: Stages 07, 11, 16, 21 and 26; review vectors, Fourier modes and validation splits.
data_role: Manufactured periodic heat-function family for actual training; a measured digit row used as an input to a constructed smoothing operator.
questions: How does a function-to-function task differ from scalar regression?
The input represents an entire field/function and the output another field/function; sampled arrays are discretizations of those objects.
What happens to the zero Fourier mode in periodic heat evolution?
Its multiplier is one, so the discrete mean is preserved.
What are the branch and trunk roles?
The branch encodes fixed input sensors into coefficients/features; the trunk maps output coordinates into features; their inner product predicts the field.
Why is the heat FFT reference not an FNO?
Its multiplier is known and fixed from the differential equation. An FNO has learned spectral weights and is trained on a mapping.
Why split whole input functions?
Grid points from one function share latent information; pointwise splitting can leak the same function across evaluation roles.
Does the real digit smoothing example validate physical heat diffusion?
No. It uses measured pixel intensities as inputs to a constructed mathematical operator, not measured later temperatures.
recall: What defines a new operator task here?
Changing input-field distribution, parameters, domain/boundary conditions, output time or observation process can change the task.
What exactly did our checkpoint selection use?
Validation-function error, not test-function error.
Why retain the analytic baseline?
The family has a known solution operator; a neural comparison without it would hide the easiest reliable solution.

title: Differentiable simulation, graph physics and attention constraints
prerequisites: Stages 16, 18, 21–28; derivatives of composed functions and causal timing.
data_role: Differentiable manufactured oscillator simulation; a graph built from an observed digit image; explicit attention and force counterexamples.
questions: What derivative does backpropagation through RK4 compute?
The derivative of the implemented finite-step RK4 computation. Agreement with the exact continuous sensitivity requires separate convergence checks.
Why is positive damping not the same as a correct physical model?
Other coefficients, forcing, observation mapping and initial conditions can be wrong; positivity enforces only one chosen restriction.
Derive zero net internal force for the pair update.
Each edge contributes F_ij and -F_ij exactly once, so its contributions cancel in the total sum.
Does zero total force imply correct acceleration for unequal masses?
No. Acceleration requires dividing each force by the corresponding mass and accounting for external terms.
What additional attention condition preserves arbitrary global sums?
Column sums must also be one; row sums alone preserve constant fields, not arbitrary totals.
What is not implemented under the physics-informed transformer heading?
No PINNsFormer paper benchmark or production transformer dynamics model is trained. The implemented experiment concerns attention and explicit conservation checks.
recall: What three checks accompany a differentiable simulation?
Numerical convergence, gradient verification and empirical validation against appropriately measured data.
Why can mean correction be insufficient?
It enforces one sum but may violate positivity, locality, energy, or other constraints.
What separates our graph example from a trained simulator?
The pair law is fixed and algebraically inspected; a learned graph model and its empirical evaluation are additional work.

title: An independent world-model study: evidence before adoption
prerequisites: All earlier selected-track stages; no need to restart stages already independently demonstrated.
data_role: An evidence audit of every new executed lab, plus a fully specified real-data regression protocol. Sports/clinical/climate validation remains a separate project.
questions: What makes a capstone question testable?
A defined prediction/measurement target, independent unit, available inputs, comparison method, evaluation protocol and decision criterion.
How do you avoid turning repeated example analysis into a new test?
Treat disclosed outcomes as exposed and obtain or preregister genuinely independent data/evaluation units before new confirmatory claims.
Can the copper data validate learned ball dynamics?
No. It is a static material-response dataset with a different observation process and target.
What information must travel with inferred sports states?
Source identities, timestamps, coordinate frame and units, observation/inference status, uncertainty, model/version and supporting evidence.
What is an acceptable negative result?
A result that fails a preregistered accuracy, uncertainty, runtime or incremental-value requirement; document it and retain the baseline rather than relabeling failure.
What remains beyond this archive?
The actual-book text audit, independent learner assessment, measured sports/clinical/climate validation, trained VGGT runs, and paper-scale reproductions explicitly marked as further work.
recall: Name the four evidence levels we keep distinct.
Algebraic/analytic checks, manufactured numerical validation, observed-data evaluation and deployment validation.
What should a source audit preserve?
The source claim, its assumptions, the independent check, supported inference and remaining limitations.
What is the next task after a failed mastery check?
Repair the specific misconception and produce new evidence; do not restart unrelated completed stages or mark it passed automatically.
